title: The 50/30/20 Budget Explained Simply (With a Real Example)

scenes.heading: Payday... gone?
lines: You get paid. Two weeks later, the money is just... gone. And you have no idea where it went.

scenes.heading: Sound familiar?
lines: Sound familiar? You're not bad with money. You just don't have a plan for it.

scenes.heading: One rule
lines: One simple rule fixes this. Fifty. Thirty. Twenty.

scenes.heading: Your numbers
lines: By the end of this video, you'll know your three numbers, down to the dollar.

scenes.heading: 3 buckets
lines: Here's the idea. You split your take-home pay into three buckets.

scenes.heading: 50% needs
lines: Fifty percent goes to needs. The stuff you must pay to live and work.

scenes.heading: 30% wants
lines: Thirty percent goes to wants. The fun stuff that makes life worth living.

scenes.heading: 20% future
lines: And twenty percent goes to your future. Savings, and crushing your debt.

scenes.heading: Who said it?
lines: It was made popular by Elizabeth Warren and her daughter Amelia, in their book All Your Worth.

scenes.heading: Take-home pay
lines: Step one. Start with your take-home pay. Not your salary.

scenes.heading: After taxes
lines: It's what actually lands in your bank account after taxes.

scenes.heading: Retirement counts
lines: If retirement money comes out of your paycheck, count it toward your twenty percent.

scenes.heading: Example
lines: Let's make it real. Say you bring home three thousand dollars a month.

scenes.heading: Needs: $1,500
lines: Fifteen hundred dollars goes to needs.

scenes.heading: Wants: $900
lines: Nine hundred dollars goes to wants.

scenes.heading: Future: $600
lines: And six hundred dollars goes to savings and extra debt payments.

scenes.heading: Done!
lines: That's it. Three numbers. Every single dollar has a job.

scenes.heading: Needs
lines: Needs are the bills you'd still pay, even in your worst month.

scenes.heading: The basics
lines: Rent or mortgage. Utilities. Basic groceries.

scenes.heading: Getting to work
lines: Getting to work. A car payment, gas, or a bus pass.

scenes.heading: Also needs
lines: Insurance, child care, and the minimum payment on every debt.

scenes.heading: Careful!
lines: But careful! Groceries are a need. Takeout is NOT.

scenes.heading: Wants
lines: Wants are everything that's nice to have, but not required.

scenes.heading: Fun money
lines: Eating out. Streaming. New clothes. Concerts. That shiny new phone.

scenes.heading: Guilt free!
lines: And here's the best part. This money is meant to be spent. Guilt free!

scenes.heading: Why it works
lines: Because a budget you actually enjoy is a budget you'll actually stick to.

scenes.heading: Future you
lines: The last twenty percent is for future you.

scenes.heading: First: safety
lines: First, build a small emergency fund, so surprises don't become new debt.

scenes.heading: Then: debt
lines: Next, attack high interest debt, like credit cards.

scenes.heading: Then: goals
lines: Then, save for retirement and your bigger goals.

scenes.heading: Reality check
lines: Now the eye opening part. Compare the plan with what you really spend.

scenes.heading: Statements
lines: Pull up your last two or three months of bank and card statements.

scenes.heading: Sort it
lines: Sort every purchase into needs, wants, or savings.

scenes.heading: Surprise!
lines: Most people are shocked. Wants hide in tiny, everyday charges.

scenes.heading: Over 50%?
lines: But what if your needs eat way more than half? This is the question I get most.

scenes.heading: Totally normal
lines: Honestly? That's really common, especially with high rent or a low income.

scenes.heading: Not a failure
lines: It doesn't mean you failed. These numbers are a target, not a law.

scenes.heading: Adjust it
lines: Try sixty, twenty, twenty for a while. Or even seventy, twenty, ten.

scenes.heading: Protect this
lines: The one thing to protect? Save something. Even if it's small.

scenes.heading: Shrink needs
lines: Then chip away at your needs, little by little.

scenes.heading: Insurance
lines: Shop around for car and renters insurance once a year.

scenes.heading: Phone plan
lines: Check a cheaper prepaid phone plan. Many cost way less than the big carriers.

scenes.heading: Cook more
lines: Cook at home more. Buy store brands for the basics.

scenes.heading: Rent
lines: And when your lease is up, think about a roommate or a cheaper place.

scenes.heading: Autopilot
lines: The secret to sticking with it? Automate everything.

scenes.heading: Pay future you
lines: On payday, move your twenty percent to savings before you can touch it.

scenes.heading: Autopay
lines: Put your bills on autopay, so your needs are always covered.

scenes.heading: Spend the rest
lines: Whatever's left in checking? That's your wants money. Enjoy it!

scenes.heading: Mistake #1
lines: Watch out for three mistakes. One: using your salary before taxes. Your numbers come out too big.

scenes.heading: Mistake #2
lines: Two: calling every want a need. Be honest with yourself.

scenes.heading: Mistake #3
lines: Three: forgetting costs that hit once or twice a year, like car repairs and gifts.

scenes.heading: Fix it
lines: Divide those by twelve, and set that amount aside every month.

scenes.heading: Recap
lines: Quick recap. Find your take-home pay. Split it fifty, thirty, twenty.

scenes.heading: Recap
lines: Check your real spending, adjust if needs run high, and automate your savings.

scenes.heading: You've got this
lines: You don't need a fancy app or a finance degree. Just three simple numbers.

scenes.heading: Next step
lines: If your twenty percent starts at zero, watch my emergency fund video next.

scenes.heading: Your turn
lines: Subscribe for one simple money move every day. And tell me your three numbers in the comments!
